title: A11y: Add aria-live announcements via @react-aria/live-announcer
body:
Storybook UI lacks a centralized approach for managing `aria-live` announcements, making screen reader users unable to perceive status changes (test results, loading states, errors, etc.). ### Changes - **`extend-to-be-announced` integration** — Added `extend-to-be-announced` (by @AriPerkkio) as a devDependency in core for robust ARIA live region assertion via `aria-live-capture`. Registered in `code/.storybook/storybook.setup.ts` via `import 'extend-to-be-announced/vitest'`. - **TestProviderRender announcements** — Integrated `announce()` from `@react-aria/live-announcer` directly into the vitest addon's `TestProviderRender` component to announce test run lifecycle events: - "Test run started." (`polite`) when tests begin - "Test run finished. X components errored, Y components with warnings, Z components passed." on completion (`assertive` if component test errors **or** accessibility errors are present, `polite` otherwise; includes a11y error/warning counts when the a11y addon is present) - "Test run crashed." (`assertive`) on fatal errors - **Stories** — 3 new stories with `play` functions on `TestProviderRender` using `render` with `useState` and mock-driven state transitions (via mocked `store.send` or `setTimeout`) to verify announcements via `waitFor` + `toBeAnnounced` (`AnnouncesTestRunStart`, `AnnouncesTestRunFinished`, `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed`). Tagged with `vitest` for vitest-only test execution. - **Dependencies** — Both `@react-aria/live-announcer` and `extend-to-be-announced` are added as devDependencies in `code/core/package.json` (required by the pre-bundling system). ### Usage ```tsx // Imperative — import directly from @react-aria/live-announcer import { announce } from '@react-aria/live-announcer'; announce('3 tests passed', 'polite'); // Test assertion (via extend-to-be-announced, registered in storybook.setup.ts) expect('3 tests passed').toBeAnnounced('polite'); expect('Error occurred').toBeAnnounced('assertive'); ``` #### Manual testing 1. **Start Storybook UI**: run `cd code && yarn storybook:ui` (requires compilation first via `yarn nx run-many -t compile -c production`) 2. **Navigate to TestProviderRender stories** — verify the `AnnouncesTestRunStart`, `AnnouncesTestRunFinished`, `AnnouncesTestRunCrashed` stories pass their play function assertions 3. **Screen reader testing**: Enable VoiceOver (⌘+F5 on macOS) and trigger test run state transitions in the announcement stories to confirm announcements are spoken
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > [A11y]: Create aria live region component > ### Describe the bug > > We need a component created to handle aria-live announcements in things like > > - [ ] the interaction addon > - [ ] the a11y addon > - [ ] the testing module > - [ ] toasts > - [ ] search > - [ ] loader > - [ ] announcing the repositioning of the addon panel > > A dedicated component will help, because live notifications often require developers to maintain a `sb-sr-only` `aria-hidden` `aria-live` UI section where they'll inject notification content. It's then necessary to clear this region so that the next notification can be sent in. > > Places where we need the component can then start using it. In some cases (search, and any classic HTML form), the live region area is not `aria-hidden` (and not `sb-sr-only`) so that it doubles up as an error notification area. The component should support both use cases. > > **The component should use react-spectrum/react-aria primitives. Do check @react-aria/live-announcer`.** > > The loader also needs to be checked for `aria-busy`. > > ### Reproduction link > > yarn storybook:ui > > ### Reproduction steps > > 1. Launch tests in the test module > 2. Turn off your screen > 3. Guess when tests are over > > ### System > > ```bash > n/a, 9.2.0 alpha > ``` > > ### Additional context > > _No response_ > > Make sure to add stories illustrating the live regions > > You may add a devDependency to detect live regions if there is a popular, maintained NPM package for it; otherwise, write a centralised test util to extend expect, so we can `expect(canvas).toHaveLiveRegion({ text: '...' })` > > Create E2E tests too > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >
- Fixes storybookjs/storybook#32251 --- 🔒 GitHub Advanced Security automatically protects Copilot coding agent pull requests. You can protect all pull requests by enabling Advanced Security for your repositories. [Learn more about Advanced Security.](https://gh.io/cca-advanced-security) ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Release Notes * **New Features** * Added live region announcements for test run state changes (start, finish, crash) to improve accessibility for screen reader users. * Introduced a new test matcher for verifying live region announcements in tests. * **Tests** * Added test stories demonstrating live region announcements for different test run scenarios.

🌐 Web query:

`@react-aria/live-announcer announce function synchronous or asynchronous`

💡 Result:

`@react-aria/live-announcer`’s `announce(...)` API is **synchronous** in the sense that it **returns `void`** (no `Promise`, not `async`). However, on the **first** call (when it has to create/attach the live region), it will often **schedule the actual DOM announcement via `setTimeout(..., 100)`** (i.e., happens asynchronously ~100ms later) to improve Safari reliability; subsequent calls announce immediately (synchronously) by directly appending to the live region. [1]

**Announcement assertions should wait for async live-region updates.**

These expectations run immediately after `mount()`. The `announce()` function from `@react-aria/live-announcer` schedules DOM updates asynchronously (~100ms on first call), so these checks can intermittently fail before the announcement is inserted into the DOM.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-import { expect, fn } from 'storybook/test';
+import { expect, fn, waitFor } from 'storybook/test';
@@
-    await expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({ text: 'Test run started.', level: 'polite' });
+    await waitFor(() =>
+      expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({ text: 'Test run started.', level: 'polite' })
+    );
@@
-    await expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({
-      text: /Test run finished\. 1 component errored, 3 components passed\./,
-      level: 'assertive',
-    });
+    await waitFor(() =>
+      expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({
+        text: /Test run finished\. 1 component errored, 3 components passed\./,
+        level: 'assertive',
+      })
+    );
@@
-    await expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({
-      text: 'Test run crashed.',
-      level: 'assertive',
-    });
+    await waitFor(() =>
+      expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({
+        text: 'Test run crashed.',
+        level: 'assertive',
+      })
+    );
```
</details>

Also applies to: 358-368, 384-394

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

In `@code/addons/vitest/src/components/TestProviderRender.stories.tsx` around
lines 337 - 345, The announcement assertions run immediately after mount but
announce() from `@react-aria/live-announcer` updates the DOM asynchronously, so
wrap the live-region expectation in an async wait helper (e.g., await waitFor(()
=> expect(document.body).toHaveLiveRegion({ text: 'Test run started.', level:
'polite' })) or use a find-style helper) to retry until the live region appears;
update each play block that mounts TestProviderRender (references: the play
function, mount, TestProviderRender, and announce) to await the waitFor-based
assertion instead of asserting immediately after mount.
```

</details>

**Reset RegExp state before `.test()` to prevent matching failures with global/sticky flags.**

When `text` is a global or sticky regex, `.test()` mutates `lastIndex`. Since this matcher loops through multiple elements, an uninitialized `lastIndex` on the second and subsequent elements can cause false negatives.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    const textMatches = typeof text === 'string' ? content.includes(text) : text.test(content);
+    const textMatches =
+      typeof text === 'string'
+        ? content.includes(text)
+        : (() => {
+            text.lastIndex = 0;
+            return text.test(content);
+          })();
```
</details>

comments.author: AriPerkkio
comments.body:
Most of these tests are passing even though they should not. Mounting a live region with text content does NOT trigger live region update in assistive technologies.

https://github.com/AriPerkkio/aria-live-capture?tab=readme-ov-file#announcement-detection-examples

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
Yeah, that helper is misleading because we check that a live region was created, not that it is announced.

The underlying expectation is that RAC's helper will maintain it and that in practice, when a live region gets created, this helper will then detect it.

So my understanding is
* testing the helper means testing that the helper detects live region
* and testing if a specific part of the UI creates a live region should be done with your code pattern (test `.not.toHaveLiveRegion` and then `.toHaveLiveRegion`)

I like your testing API in your addon and I think it's kinda nicer, though don't think it goes well with RAC, because I believe RAC maintains a single live region in the entire app.

Would you be ok to give this PR a thorough review and tell me if you think the API makes sense for checking if we're correctly using @react-aria/live-announcer?

Reviewed rest of the code ✅ 

> though don't think it goes well with RAC, because I believe RAC maintains a single live region in the entire app

That should not matter at all. It's all about detecting DOM updates in whole document.
